articles.title: Stop Using chmod 777 for One Extra User: Practical POSIX ACLs on Linux
articles.excerpt: A deploy user needs to write to one directory owned by a service account. The ticket is two lines long. The fastest fix is chmod 777, and it works right up until someone asks who else can write there.…
articles.body: A deploy user needs to write to one directory owned by a service account. The ticket is two lines long. The fastest fix is chmod 777 , and it works right up until someone asks who else can write there. The second-fastest fix is to add the user to the directory's group. That also works, with two side effects people forget: group membership is host-wide, so the user now has that group's access to every file the group owns, and supplementary groups are resolved at login, so the change may not apply to the session that is currently running. POSIX ACLs exist for exactly this case: a per-object grant to a named user or group, without changing ownership or opening the file to everyone.

articles.title: pam_exec environment data is not a safe secret channel
articles.excerpt: pam_exec environment data is not a safe secret channel pam_exec runs an external command during a PAM module stage. It is available for authentication, account, password, and session processing. It al…
articles.body: pam_exec environment data is not a safe secret channel pam_exec runs an external command during a PAM module stage. It is available for authentication, account, password, and session processing. It also exports PAM items as environment variables and can expose the authentication token when configured to do so. Those features make it useful for integration and dangerous when the called program is not treated as privileged code. The manual lists items such as PAM_RHOST , PAM_RUSER , PAM_SERVICE , and PAM_TTY among the exported environment. A helper may use them to decide how to log a login, notify a system, or apply a session policy. The values can still be influenced by the client or the service configuration.

articles.title: Lazarus Group: the hackers who fund a nation
articles.excerpt: Most hackers want money. Some want attention. A few want secrets. Lazarus Group wants all three, and it has something no ransomware gang will ever have: a country standing behind it. I spend a lot of…
articles.body: Most hackers want money. Some want attention. A few want secrets. Lazarus Group wants all three, and it has something no ransomware gang will ever have: a country standing behind it. I spend a lot of my time studying how real attacks actually happen, because that is the only honest way to defend what I build. And no name shows up more often behind the biggest heists of the last decade than this one. Who they are "Lazarus" is the umbrella name researchers use for hacking units run by North Korea. Governments, including the United States, attribute them to the country's intelligence apparatus. You will also see names like APT38, TraderTraitor or BlueNoroff. They are sub-teams, specialised by mission. What makes them different is the goal. Most state hackers steal secrets.

articles.body: Meta title: CI/CD Pipeline Design Improvement Roadmap Meta description: Follow a practical CI/CD pipeline design improvement roadmap to identify bottlenecks, optimize workflows, strengthen security, and improve delivery performance. A CI/CD pipeline improvement roadmap helps engineering teams make software delivery faster, more reliable, and more secure without adding unnecessary complexity. The most effective approach is to measure the current pipeline, identify the biggest bottlenecks, prioritize changes by impact, and validate each improvement against delivery performance and cost. The goal is not simply to reduce pipeline runtime. A pipeline that finishes faster but misses tests, produces inconsistent builds, or makes deployments riskier is not an improvement.

articles.body: Ahead of the release of Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI , Nintendo is launching its own fall juggernaut: a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. Nintendo has also launched a special version of the Switch 2 and Switch 2 Pro Controller with Triforce imagery to celebrate the game.

articles.body: NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now. The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way. articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

articles.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
articles.excerpt: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart.
articles.body: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement .
